narrative.northStar: 纸面工作台 / The Paper Workbench
narrative.overview: AllJobs behaves like an editorial planning workbench where Backlog and Task ledgers own the primary reading plane. Derived from the disciplined typography and tactile paper aesthetic of pleurat.com, it uses warm cream paper grounds, deep ink typography, and a signature amber provenance status bar. External read-only sources are marked with hatch fills; native writable objects are marked with solid ink fills. All decorative star atlases, celestial charts, and dashboard card walls are firmly rejected.
keyCharacteristics: Ledger-first information density dominating the visual plane.
Warm cream paper tonal layers (#F1EEE6 / #FBF7E6) with crisp hairline rules.
Amber provenance status bar binding route, custody, digest, and freshness on every view.
General Sans for human discourse, IBM Plex Mono for technical coordinates and provenance.
Hatch pattern for external read-only projections, solid ink for native writable objects.

rules.name: The Amber Provenance Rule
rules.body: Amber is strictly reserved for the provenance status bar, primary confirmed actions, and active indicators; rust marks attention or failure, and every state requires explicit text.

rules.name: The Dual-Type Rule
rules.body: General Sans carries human narrative and work titles; IBM Plex Mono carries technical custody, file paths, hashes, and machine-verified states.

rules.name: The Ledger-First Rule
rules.body: Backlog and Task content receives the majority of available width and appears before provenance or roadmap context at every breakpoint.

rules.name: The Tactile Workbench Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest flat with hairline rules; depth is established through tonal layering and a 2px hover lift; shadows are reserved for Human Gate modals.

rules.name: The Provenance Hatching Rule
rules.body: Hatch patterns represent external read-only custody; solid fills represent AllJobs-native writable custody.

dos: Do make Backlog and Task ledgers the dominant visual plane on every screen.
Do bind every view to the amber provenance status bar showing exact source custody, revision, and digest.
Do distinguish external read-only projections (hatch fill / dashed badge) from native writable objects (solid fill).
Do preserve full copy, error reasons, and disabled explanations in text, not color alone.
Do provide smooth prefers-reduced-motion fallbacks for all transitions.
donts: Don't include decorative star atlases, celestial charts, galaxy canvases, or dot-grid diagrams.
Don't use card grids or floating dashboard widgets that fragment linear reading.
Don't use gradient text, decorative glassmorphism, or dark nocturnal themes in revision 3.
Don't shrink desktop tables on mobile into horizontally unreadable clipping containers.
Don't execute canonical writes or bypass the explicit Human Gate confirmation boundary.
